In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis, and application of recoverable organic catalyst bearing ionic liquid (ROCI) moieties for regio-, stereo-, enantio-, and diastereoselective reactions of carbon acid derivatives.

the development of recoverable organic catalyst bearing IL moieties for the regio-, stereo-, or enantioselectivity controlled reactions of carbon acids, and the mechanistic understanding of their catalytic action.

these new IL-based catalysts have the same potential for use in chemical reactions of carbon acids as the traditional catalysts, and they have the additional advantage of being readily recyclable and hence available for use in multiple cycles of chemical reactions.
these new IL-based organic catalysts are a very promising class of compounds with the potential to become the new standard for many important organic reactions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed new classes of organic catalysts that can be recovered by simple filtration or centrifugation.
IL-based PTCs and organocatalysts are promising catalysts for the reactions of carbon acids.

the IL moieties are able to stabilize reactive intermediates such as carbanions and anions of enols, and to facilitate their reactions with electrophiles, and that they are also able to prevent the undesired reactions of the reactive intermediates with water and oxygen, which are present in the aqueous phase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of organic cations with bulky and rigid structures, combined with fluorinated anions, is crucial for the development of recoverable organic catalyst systems with high catalytic efficiency.
the combination of IL moieties with bulky organic cations can lead to catalysts that are highly efficient and can catalyze reactions in organic solvents.
ILs can be used to develop new organic catalysts with unique properties, such as recoverability, that are not possible with conventional organic catalysts.
